_why: Mocked shopper relationships, one roster per merchant. There is no OAuth here and the demo does not pretend otherwise -- what is being demonstrated is what an agent may do with a linked identity, not how the link is established. The roster is per-merchant on purpose: membership is not a global fact about a shopper, it is something each merchant knows about its own customers, which is why it belongs behind that merchant's signature and not in the agent's wallet.

_states.member: has an existing relationship -- earns the loyalty record
_states.prospect: known to the merchant, no orders yet -- earns the acquisition record
_states.absent: not in the roster at all -- sees only the universal records

northgear._why_empty: NorthGear's 20%-off promotion is a public banner addressed to anyone, so it is published with shopper_id '*' and needs no roster entry. That is the point of the contrast: the offer that asks for none of the shopper's data is also the one that turns out to be worth nothing here.

citycircuit._why_empty: The control keeps no agent-readable shopper relationship, the same way it publishes no benefit extension. Status quo, not a strawman.
